open_obligations: Check whether Sudhir et al.'s NaiveJudge baseline corresponds to Kenton et al.'s direct QA baselines.
Check whether Sudhir et al.'s alignment measure coincides with judge accuracy for the protocols compared.
Note the small demonstration scale (100 questions, one judge).

Note that Kenton et al. say their findings only apply in the inference-only setting and that a proper evaluation of protocols used for training may reveal other findings, while in Sudhir et al. Propaganda simulates a reinforcement learning from human feedback setting and NaiveJudge a supervised learning setting in which the agent is scored on its agreement with the judge; the cited Sudhir et al. lines show no fine-tuning of the judge, which Kenton et al. suspect may help debate improve over direct QA baselines.
out.other_title: Can debate with weak judges beat direct QA baselines, e.g. via judge fine-tuning?
out.rationale: Kenton et al. name showing debate improves over direct QA baselines as a key challenge. Sudhir et al. report Debate outperforms all other tested protocols on inducing alignment (Figure 1) and on Expected Judge Score; the tested protocols include NaiveJudge, in which the judge does not give feedback based on the agent's response but reports its probability independently, as well as Propaganda and Consultancy. The alignment measure is not shown to be judge accuracy, and the results are on 100 GSM8K questions with one judge.
out.scope: proposed ADDRESSES: whether debate outperforms other tested protocols, including a judge-alone baseline (NaiveJudge), for GSM8K with a gpt-4o-mini judge
